questions.question: Post and balance the Debtors Control account for August using the lesson's figures, stating each entry's side and contra account.
questions.expected_answer: Debit side: Balance b/d R18 700 and Sales (Debtors Journal total) R52 600 — total R71 300. Credit side: Bank R36 400 (payments received), Debtors Allowances R3 100 (returns), Bad Debts R1 200 (write-off) — total R40 700. Balance c/d R30 600 on the credit side, brought down as Balance b/d R30 600 on the debit side: debtors owe the business R30 600.

questions.question: Explain why writing off a bad debt credits the control account even though no money was received.
questions.expected_answer: The credit side records everything that makes debtors owe less. When a debt is written off, the business stops claiming that money — the asset is removed and the loss is absorbed as the Bad Debts expense. Debtors as a group now owe less, so control is credited; prudence demands the asset not be overstated by keeping an uncollectable debt on the books.

questions.question: Describe how the agreement check works and what a disagreement of R1 200 between the list and the control balance would suggest in this month's figures.
questions.expected_answer: At month end the individual balances in the Debtors Ledger are listed and totalled; the total must equal the control balance of R30 600 because both records were built from the same transactions along independent roads. A R1 200 gap matches the bad debt written off, suggesting the write-off reached the control totals but was never posted to the customer's personal account — fix the page and the counts agree.
